The precisely scoped mathematical manuscript passes. This does not complete original P19.2. R, T and C were used only within their caller-granted domains; historical verdicts, the ledger and round140 were not treated as additional grants.

The relative-ceiling lemma has a valid direct Perron proof. For each competitor h, the subgeodesic max(u_s,h+λs) lies between u_s and u_s+C, so its slices have finite energy even when h does not. Its boundary upper values are bounded by w and u_T+C. The canonical comparison geodesic is u_s+Cs/T. Taking T→∞ establishes h≤χ. The argument assumes the stated genuine psh level and imports no minimum principle. The decreasing-level identity follows by commuting the two infima; it supplies no general mass or entropy continuity.

The geometric construction is actual. The sections generate the ideal (Z₀,τ), whose pullback is O(−E). The twisted Rees algebra gives the claimed closed graph embedding and g*O(1)=T−E. For s=A/M, both factors of O(M−A,A) are positive, so their projective embeddings establish relative ampleness near zero; locality on the base handles the compactification. The fixed factor is precisely O(−AE). I independently checked both time multiplicities, the exceptional discrepancy, the restrictions to F₀ and E, and the binomial intersections. These yield the probability masses aⁿ and 1−aⁿ, e_s=(1−aⁿ⁺¹)/(n+1)−s, and h_s=1−aⁿ. The generator calculation includes supported semivaluations. Uniform error 1−s and the granted energy foundations establish strong convergence.

The singular conjugate is correct, including F_w(0)=+∞, the critical point −(3x)⁻³ᐟ², and the derivative jump at δ. The bounded regularization decreases: increasing m decreases the soft-maximum scale and its second input. Its conjugates increase to F_w, with F_m(0)=m. The optimizer-exclusion argument prevents spurious limiting mass at moment zero. Each approximating ray is bounded on finite annuli. Away from p and H its matching first derivatives and locally bounded Hessian identify the Bedford–Taylor product with the almost-everywhere determinant; the hinge produces a plateau. Bounded products charge neither analytic set. Thus these are bounded homogeneous geodesics. Perron comparison, the sandwich w−st≤b≤w and decreasing finite-energy continuity establish the actual limiting geodesics, their endpoints and strong time continuity. No unbounded Bedford–Taylor continuity is assumed.

The Gauss calculation uses generic divisorial asymptotics. Fixing a positive moment before taking the time limit correctly avoids evaluating F_w(0)/t or w(p)/t. Subtracting the reference coefficient gives exactly −s min(v(H),1). Divisorial determination is applied within R's stated scope. The moment probability n xⁿ⁻¹dx gives the energy derivative e_s; decreasing energy continuity passes this identity through the bounded approximants. The zero-defect criterion therefore establishes maximality, including s=1. Order and the ordered d₁ identity prove (10).

Every closed Legendre case is covered: λ≤−s gives w; genuine intermediate levels give V_d; λ=0 with a>0 gives V_a; and a=λ=0 gives the actual identically minus-infinite level. Positive λ also gives that placeholder. The constrained radial weights are globally psh, retain w near p and have hyperplane coefficient 1−d. Their relative ceilings follow from the direct lemma. Polarization gives the mixed distribution d(Q_d′ᵏQ₀′ⁿ⁻ᵏ), with no interface atom; excluding the polar divisorial contribution leaves raw mass dᵏ. This proves the decreasing boundary convergence and the uniform k/j bounds. The ordered metric formula applies only to genuine levels, using V_d/(2π) with background ω. It gives (16) and n/(2j) for λ<0. No metric, current, probability measure or degree-zero mass is assigned to the minus-infinite placeholder. [DDNL, v1, Lemma 3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.00839v1).

The entropy density and shift calculation in (17) are correct. Plateaus have zero top mass, and the transported top measure remains a probability. The remainder lies between log p_w and zero. Its negative tail is O(xⁿ⁻⁵ᐟ²), including the integrable x⁻¹ᐟ² tail when n=2. Consequently B_n is finite, every finite-time entropy is finite, and (13) controls every joint index/time limit without invoking entropy continuity for arbitrary strongly convergent sequences.

The general mechanism is stated accurately. Equation (19) uses a genuine common upper maximal ray, the supporting inequality and fixed-measure integrability from R. It establishes bounded-time d₁ recovery and the stated individual slopes. Convexity of the extended Mabuchi functional establishes finite intermediate entropy. For a nonmaximal ray, energy affinity and the 1-Lipschitz energy bound give (20), with limiting lower bound δ>0. This limits that maximal-ray mechanism; it establishes no universal approximation obstruction or prescribed-boundary recovery.

The displayed toric diagnostic is independently verified within T's zero-start curve scope. All lengths are positive, the rays (1,i) form a regular chain, the multiplicities are i, and the component degrees are 1−c_j and a_i/i. The monomial ideal and divisor factors agree. R_j→0, energy→0 and the uniform entropy remainder hold, while every fixed negative level eventually equals zero. The genuine endpoint instead has mass 1/j and distance c_j/2 from the trivial endpoint. The product sequence demonstrates why this is an implication failure. The two-moment arithmetic is valid for positive residual roof moments: its coefficients are (R′−T′/N)/(1/m−1/N) and (T′/m−R′)/(1/m−1/N). No infinite-chain analytic theorem is promoted. C supplies only its stated absolute-endpoint counterexample.

The source comparisons also hold. DXZ's model levels use the absolute ceiling and its positive-mass initial limit is model. DZ's recovery theorem concerns polarized, zero-start finite-radial-entropy rays, and its log-discrepancy bundles need not be relatively semiample. MP's mixed estimate requires mean-zero slots and relative J; constant shifts cannot be silently substituted into d₁. MPWN's complete Theorem 9.2.1 proof uses dual-complex measures, Calabi–Yau recovery and PL obstacles. None supplies the additional relative-boundary conclusions disclaimed here. Pertinent statement and proof units were read, including DDNL's preceding energy construction and the complete DZ Theorem 10.1 proof. [MPWN, v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.09442v1).

Harmless clarifications: the gradient in §4.2 is (x,−(x−a)₊) in coordinates (ρ,t), and (x,(x−a)₊) in (ρ,log|τ|²); the determinant argument is unchanged. The C¹ assertion for Q_m concerns the radial variable, not global C¹ regularity at p. DZ's zero-start qualification should be explicit. None requires a substantial repair. Artifact, compilation and historical-provenance statements were not used as mathematical evidence.

passages.statement: Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Theorems 2.1 and 6.9: mixed products of locally bounded psh functions are weakly continuous under decreasing sequences having locally bounded limits. Pluripolar subsets of strongly pseudoconvex domains have zero outer Bedford–Taylor capacity; locally bounded psh Monge–Ampère measures therefore do not charge pluripolar sets.

passages.statement: On a smooth compact Kähler manifold, the weak geodesic between bounded ω-psh endpoints is the Perron envelope of subgeodesics whose boundary upper limits are dominated by the endpoints, and is the unique bounded invariant homogeneous Monge–Ampère solution with those boundary values. For arbitrary ω-psh endpoints, decreasing bounded endpoint approximations give the same Perron envelope whenever their limit is genuine. Darvas, arXiv:1401.7318v3, Sections 2.2 and 5; Berndtsson, arXiv:1103.0923v3, Section 2.2.
